title: Dimension of a formal monoid ring and a parameter hypersurface
statement:
Let $(D,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero complete regular Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and $T$ a fine saturated sharp monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively; sharp means that its only invertible element is $0$. Let $D[T]$ be the ring with $D$-basis $[t]$, $t\in T$, and multiplication $[t][u]=[t+u]$. Put $\mathfrak a=(\mathfrak m,[t]:t\ne0)\subset D[T]$, let $H=\varprojlim_jD[T]/\mathfrak a^j$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $L=([t]:t\in T\setminus\{0\})H$. Then $H$ is a Noetherian local integral domain, $H/L\cong D$, and
$$\dim H=\dim D+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{\rm gp}.$$
Furthermore, for every $\eta\in H$ whose reduction $\overline\eta\in H/L=D$ belongs to $\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$, multiplication by $\eta$ on $H$ is injective, $D/(\overline\eta)$ is regular local, and
$$\dim(H/(\eta))=\dim D+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{\rm gp}-1,\qquad \dim(D/(\overline\eta))=\dim D-1.$$
Dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; the zero-rank monoid $T=\{0\}$ is allowed.

proof.text: Put $d=\dim D$ and $r=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{\rm gp}$. The singleton $F=\{0\}$ is a face of $T$: if $u+v=0$, both terms are units and hence zero. Apply [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] with $Q=T$, $F=\{0\}$. Its localization and quotient are just $T$, so $G=T^{\rm gp}$ is free abelian of finite rank $r$. Since $T$ is sharp, $T\cap(-T)=\{0\}$ inside $G$. Apply [lem-trf-sharp-monoid-positive-grading] to choose $w:G\to\mathbf Z$ positive on every nonzero element of $T$. Choose nonzero generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ of $T$ (the list is empty for $T=\{0\}$).

source.place: VI 1.6 sharp fs monoid; VIII 3.1.1 and 3.1.10; positive-weight refinement.

proof.text: The map $D[X_1,\ldots,X_s]\to D[T]$, $X_i\mapsto[g_i]$, is surjective: every basis monomial is a product of the chosen generators. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $D[T]$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] makes $H$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-monoid-completion-coefficients] with $A=D$, $P=T$ and the weight of step 1. We may now write every element of $H$ uniquely as a family $\sum_t a_t[t]$, with the convolution rule, and use its exact formula for $\mathfrak a^nH$. In particular $D$ embeds as the constant families. All the coefficient lemma hypotheses hold: $D$ is complete separated Noetherian local, $T$ is finitely generated and embeds in the finite free group just obtained.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 0316, lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian; VI 1.6 coefficient refinement.

proof.text: Constant coefficient $c:H\to D$ is a surjective ring map: sharpness implies $u+v=0$ only for $u=v=0$. Its kernel is $L$. Indeed, partition $T\setminus\{0\}$ into $s$ subsets by choosing, for each $t$, one generator $g_i$ with $t-g_i\in T$. For a family with $a_0=0$, assign $a_t[t-g_i]$ to the corresponding family $f_i$. The coefficient description gives $f_i\in H$ and $f=\sum_i[g_i]f_i$; conversely every such sum has zero constant coefficient. Hence $H/L\cong D$. A family with unit constant coefficient is a unit: after factoring that coefficient, write it as $1+h$ with $h\in L$, and $\sum_{j\ge0}(-h)^j$ converges since $h^j\in\mathfrak a^jH$; multiplication of partial sums gives its inverse. A unit must have unit constant coefficient by applying $c$. Thus the nonunits form $\mathfrak n=c^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$. The coefficient formula for $n=1$ identifies $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak aH$, so $H$ is local with residue field $D/\mathfrak m$. This argument includes $s=0$, when $H=D$ and $L=0$.

source.place: VI 1.6: direct constant-coefficient and geometric-series computation in the formal models.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], $D$ is an integral domain. Choose coordinates $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$ and order $G$ lexicographically by $(w(t),t_1,\ldots,t_r)$; this is an addition-invariant total order. Each set $\{t\in T:w(t)\le B\}$ is finite: a generator expression has at most $B$ terms because every $w(g_i)\ge1$. Hence every nonempty subset of $T$ has a least element in this order. If $f,g\in H$ are nonzero, let $u,v$ be their least exponents with nonzero coefficient. In the convolution coefficient at $u+v$, any nonzero term has exponents $u'\ge u$ and $v'\ge v$; if either inequality is strict, addition invariance gives $u'+v'>u+v$. Consequently the coefficient there is exactly $a_ub_v\ne0$. Thus $fg\ne0$, proving that $H$ is a nonzero integral domain.

source.place: VI 1.6: least-monomial argument; regular-domain input Stacks Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain.

proof.text:
Write $
u(t)$ for the order in [lem-trf-monoid-completion-coefficients] and $\ell_D(k)=\mathrm{length}_D(D/\mathfrak m^k)$ for $k\ge1$. For fixed $n$, the set $S_n=\{t:
u(t)<n\}$ is finite, and the coefficient lemma gives the quotient coefficients $D/\mathfrak m^{n-
u(t)}$. Order $S_n$ by the addition-invariant order in step 4. The submodules of $H/\mathfrak n^n$ supported on successive final segments give a finite filtration: multiplication by any nonzero monomial strictly raises the exponent, and coefficients outside $S_n$ vanish. The factor for $t$ is $D/\mathfrak m^{n-
u(t)}$, with $H$ acting by constant coefficient. Its $H$-submodules are exactly its $D$-submodules, since $D\subset H$ acts by all scalars and every $h$ acts by $c(h)$. Therefore repeated length additivity [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] gives
$$\mathrm{length}_H(H/\mathfrak n^n)=\sum_{
u(t)<n}\ell_D(n-
u(t)).$$
Each summand is finite: [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-growth-dimension] gives finiteness for large powers, and smaller quotients are surjective images of those (a submodule chain lifts under a surjection).

source.place: Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive; Tag 00K8, proposition-hilbert-function-polynomial; VI 1.6 monomial filtration computation.

proof.text:
First suppose $r>0$. Put $M=\max_i w(g_i)\ge1$. For every $t$, each decomposition into nonzero terms has length at most $w(t)$, whereas any expression in the generators has length at least $w(t)/M$. Hence
$$w(t)/M\le\nu(t)\le w(t).$$
In fixed lattice coordinates let $C\ge1$ bound all $|(g_i)_j|$. If $\nu(t)<n$, a generator expression has fewer than $n$ terms, so every coordinate of $t$ has absolute value at most $Cn$. The injective lattice coordinates bound $|S_n|\le(2Cn+1)^r$. All summands in step 5 are at most $\ell_D(n)$ because reduction from $D/\mathfrak m^n$ is surjective. The Hilbert--Samuel theorem applied to $D$ gives positive constants $b,B$ with $b k^d\le\ell_D(k)\le B k^d$ for all sufficiently large $k$. Thus step 5 is bounded above by a constant times $n^{d+r}$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, with Tag 00K8; elementary upper bound on monomial counts.

proof.text: The generators span $G\otimes\mathbf Q$, so select $r$ linearly independent ones $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ by finite-dimensional elimination. Put $W=\max_j w(v_j)$. The elements $t=\sum_j b_jv_j$ for $0\le b_j\le\lfloor n/(4rW)\rfloor$ are distinct, and satisfy $\nu(t)\le w(t)\le n/4$. There are $(\lfloor n/(4rW)\rfloor+1)^r$ of them, bounded below by a positive constant times $n^r$. Each contributes at least $\ell_D(\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$ to step 5. The lower Hilbert--Samuel bound of step 6 therefore gives a positive constant times $n^{d+r}$. Apply [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-growth-dimension] also to the nonzero Noetherian local ring $H$. Its length polynomial has positive leading coefficient; the two bounds force its degree to be exactly $d+r$ (a polynomial of degree $e$ grows between positive multiples of $n^e$). Its degree is $\dim H$, so $\dim H=d+r$. For $r=0$, the injection $T\hookrightarrow G=0$ gives $T=\{0\}$ and step 3 gives $H=D$, proving the same equality without choosing $M,W$ or dividing by $r$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, with Tag 00K8; elementary lower monomial count and comparison of polynomial degrees.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be as in the statement and put $f=c(\eta)\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$. Then $f\ne0$, hence $\eta\ne0$, and the domain result of step 4 makes multiplication by $\eta$ injective. Since $\mathfrak n=c^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$, $\eta\in\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] to $(H,\mathfrak n)$ and $\eta$ to obtain $\dim(H/(\eta))+1=\dim H=d+r$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] to $(D,\mathfrak m)$ and $f$ to obtain that $D/(f)$ is regular local. Finally $D$ is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], so its nonzero element $f$ is a nonzerodivisor; the same dimension-drop node applied to $D$ gives $\dim(D/(f))+1=d$. These are the two claimed formulas. If $d=0$, $D$ is a field and $\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$ is empty, so this universal assertion has no instances; no negative dimension of a nonzero ring is asserted.
